speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you're experiencing knee pain after increasing your physical activity; to help me pinpoint the cause, could you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it worsens with specific movements like walking or climbing stairs?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the history of volleyball with repetitive pivoting and the sudden onset of worsening pain, can you describe the exact location of the pain (e.g., inner, outer, front, or back of the knee) and whether you heard or felt a "pop" when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splains)

The pain location you described over the medial tibia, combined with recent increased physical activity and weight loss attempts, is highly suggestive of Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome. While I cannot request images directly, do you have any visible swelling or bruising on the shin, and does pressing directly on the bone along the inner edge of your tibia cause sharp pain?
